artificial-superintelligence: A wide, forward-tilting illustration shows an ascending staircase of three glowing machines rising from left to right against a dark sky: on the lowest step, a small, single-purpose robot absorbed in one narrow task; on the middle step, a humanoid machine standing level with a human figure beside it, labeled "AGI"; and on the top step, a radiant, incomprehensibly complex entity of light and circuitry towering far above the human, radiating outward in every direction — symbols of an atom, a chessboard, a speech scroll, and a lightbulb orbiting its halo to show mastery of science, strategy, persuasion, and invention all at once. Below the staircase, at ground level, several rival corporate logos and national flags race side by side along a track heading straight toward the staircase's base, each ignoring warning signs and a broken fence marked "safety checks," while a small group of worried researchers stands at the side holding question-mark-shaped tools, unable to verify or halt the runners — the whole scene hovering in a dreamlike haze to underline that the topmost figure remains hypothetical.
frontier-ai-lab: A wide, dimly lit landscape illustration shows four colossal glass-and-steel structures rising from a windswept plain at the edge of a map that simply dissolves into blank space beyond them — the visible frontier. The buildings are racing: they lean forward at slight angles like sprinters, connected by a tangle of luminous tracks that converge toward the empty horizon, and each structure is fed by rivers of gold coins pouring in through pipes from the edges of the frame. Inside the largest building, through transparent walls, an enormous glowing neural network pulses with new, unexpected shapes — small wings and eyes budding spontaneously from its nodes, while its tiny human engineers stare up in alarm, some pressing hands to the glass. Most striking, several workers have stepped outside the buildings entirely, standing alone in the cold to hold up warning signs with exclamation marks, their silhouettes dwarfed by the towers yet lit by the very glow of the systems they are cautioning the world about.
necessity-defence: The illustration shows a climate protester standing in the middle of a highway, chained to a toppled barricade, calmly raising one hand in confession while with the other arm holding back a colossal wall of floodwater and flame that looms over the town behind her—the visible greater harm she says her trespass prevented. Facing her, a towering judicial bench shaped like an immense set of scales weighs her small broken barricade on one pan against the roaring disaster on the other, but the beam of the scales is suspended far above a horizontal bar drawn across the image at head height, so that neither pan can reach it: this is the imminence-and-proportionality threshold, marked "no reasonable legal alternative," which the defense almost never clears. In the foreground, a police officer approaches with handcuffs, and a gavel already rests on the ground beside her feet; a thin dotted line traces from the protester's honest, open heart to the courthouse and then drops straight into a jail cell, showing that even when the motive is sincere and the harm real, a failed necessity defence leaves the conviction untouched. The overall composition splits into two registers—warm civic colors on the side of the rescued town, cold institutional blues around the bench—to make clear at a glance that the entry is about the law's reluctant, rarely granted excuse for breaking a law to stop a bigger harm.
